clue.text: Films a bird no longer found in Pacific Islands

blocks.note: westerns are cowboy films
taken as written
the moa was a huge flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct

explanation.surface: A wildlife film crew reports that a certain bird has vanished from the islands of the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer found' reads as part of the surface story; 'no longer' marks the bird as extinct, and 'found in' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Western Samoa was the name of the independent island nation in the South Pacific before it became plain Samoa in 1997.

clue.text: Go swiftly round a very quiet bit of the Thames

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the outer word wraps the inner pieces

blocks.note: to wing is to fly fast
taken as written
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: Someone races round a peaceful stretch of the river in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping is a district on the north bank of the Thames in east London, where The Times itself moved in 1986.
explanation.definitionFit: Wapping is a riverside district lying along the Thames in London's East End, so it is a stretch of that river's bank.

clue.text: Preserve, in a way, what's in short supply

definitions.note: a phrase for something scarce; the answer is the adjective meaning scarce

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the second word holds the first

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it in a tin
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A question about what makes a good preserve when supplies run low.
explanation.walkthrough: The page split this clue across two columns, so the source lost its last words, 'short supply'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant describes a quantity that is barely enough or lacking, which is exactly how something in short supply is.

clue.text: Issuing novel half-heartedly to people

indicators.note: doing something half-heartedly here means losing half of the heart, one of the two middle letters

blocks.note: Emma is the Jane Austen novel
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A writer half-heartedly releases a new novel to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective or a hint to shuffle letters; it is a particular novel, EMMA, whose double M at the heart loses one.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that issues or flows out from a source, so the noun matches issuing used as a noun.

clue.text: Final cricket practice before start of test

indicators.note: one piece coming before another simply means it is written first, the next one following
the start of a word is its opening letter, the one kept here

blocks.note: a practice session in the mesh enclosure where cricketers bat and bowl
the opening letter of test

explanation.surface: A cricketer has a last session in the nets before a Test match begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' looks like it describes the practice; it is the definition. Nets are the enclosures where cricketers practise batting and bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Nett, the British spelling of net, describes the final amount left after all deductions, as in a nett price or nett result.

clue.text: I play-act in a way that's unusual

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the raw material

explanation.surface: An actor admits that their way of performing is out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, departing from the normal pattern, which is what unusual says.

clue.text: Volunteer unavailable to king

blocks.note: a dish that is off is no longer available
ER is Edward Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Someone offers their services to a monarch who will not receive them.
explanation.walkthrough: ER usually means the Queen, but it stands just as well for Edward Rex, any King Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to put it forward freely without being asked, which is what offering it means.

clue.text: So-called novelist in county set

blocks.note: first meaning: the forename of the novelist W. ... Maugham, the name he was known by
second meaning: an English county in the south-west

explanation.surface: A writer with a pen name has set his book among the gentry of a shire.
explanation.walkthrough: Maugham was christened William but known by his middle name, hence 'so-called'. Somerset is a rural county in south-west England; 'set' says the novelist is placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset was the name W. Somerset Maugham went by, and it is also a county of south-west England.

clue.text: Boss one follows round the workplace

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so these pieces are written after the first in turn

blocks.note: a boss is a raised stud or knob
the Roman numeral for one
a round shape, the letter O

explanation.surface: An employee trails the manager as they go round the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' wants to be the manager; it is the ornamental knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is the working room of an artist, photographer or broadcaster, so it is a kind of workplace.

clue.text: Yokels left out of joke

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it, leaving the rest behind

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a pleasantry is a light joke

explanation.surface: Country folk have been excluded from the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasantry is the collective word for rural labourers, and yokels is a mocking name for country people as a group.

clue.text: Poet's rhyme, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak tells you to take the word by its sound, as if spoken, not by its spelling

blocks.note: first meaning: the American poet who wrote 'The Road Not Taken'
second meaning: said out loud this word is rime, a coating of ice crystals

explanation.surface: A question about what a poet's rhymes really amount to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's rhyme' reads as one phrase about verse; the poet and the spoken word are separate halves. Rime is a white coating of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Frost was the New England poet, and rime, which is pronounced like rhyme, is a feathery icy coating, a kind of hoar frost.

clue.text: Place for arriving mail train, perhaps, at journey's end

indicators.note: perhaps says the word is only possibly in this form, so its letters may be rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of journey

explanation.surface: The mail arrives by train, its trip over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail train' looks like a single phrase; the mail belongs to the definition and the train to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray is the tray on an office desk where incoming letters and papers are placed until they are dealt with.

clue.text: A couple of birds died in part of harbour

blocks.note: first bird: a pie is a magpie
second bird: the rhea is a large flightless South American bird
d is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Two seabirds were found dead down at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie, for magpie, is an old word the crossword keeps alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierhead is the outer, seaward end of a pier, which is a structure forming part of a harbour.

clue.text: Breather that's a help for hunter

blocks.note: a fish breathes through its gills
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A short rest gives a hunter some relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' wants to mean a rest; it is the organ a fish breathes with. A gillie is a Scottish hunting or fishing guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is an attendant who assists a sportsman on a Scottish estate, guiding hunting and fishing parties.

clue.text: A few lines from somewhere in Ireland

blocks.note: first meaning: a comic five-line verse
second meaning: a city and county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone sends a short note from a place in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A few lines' reads as a letter or postcard; it is a verse form named after the Irish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is a humorous poem of five lines, and Limerick is a city on the Shannon in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Male pride is keeping physicist and doctor apart

indicators.note: keeping things apart means standing between them, so this sits inside the outer letters

blocks.note: Ernst Mach, the Austrian physicist of the Mach number
taken as written
MO is a Medical Officer

explanation.surface: Masculine ego is the thing stopping a scientist and a doctor from getting along.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is an exaggerated sense of masculine pride and toughness, from the Spanish word for manly.

clue.text: Bravery of novelist, say, and poet

indicators.note: say asks you to speak the word, keeping its sound but not its spelling

blocks.note: Thomas Hardy, the novelist, spoken
Thomas Hood, the Victorian poet

explanation.surface: A tribute to the courage shown by a novelist and a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Both writers are Thomases: Hardy the novelist and Hood the comic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness and daring, the quality of being hardy in spirit, so it is a synonym for courage.

clue.text: Standard-bearing cavalryman, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: one thing bearing another carries it in front, so that piece is written first

blocks.note: par is the standard score
a lance was a mounted soldier armed with one, a lancer

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier carries the regimental flag, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard-bearing' looks like one word for a flag-carrier; the standard is golf's par, carried ahead of the horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of talking or idiom, as in common parlance, which is a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Folk song about Northern European

definitions.note: Armenia lies on the border of Europe and Asia

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for the music wraps the word for the people

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
folk are people, men
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A folk song is written about someone from northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folk song' looks like one phrase; folk and song are separate pieces, and 'Northern' is not attached to European.
explanation.definitionFit: An Armenian is a native of Armenia, a Caucasus nation often counted as European in culture and politics.

clue.text: Undertake to offer us same arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to give us the same deal as before.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a duty or responsibility is to take it on, which is what undertaking it means.

clue.text: In German capital, strike breaker is escaping charge

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its capital letter, the one at its head

blocks.note: the capital letter of German
a rat is a worker who breaks a strike
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' looks like Berlin or Bonn; it is the first letter of the word German.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge, and something that escapes a charge costs nothing.

clue.text: Notice about spirit inside — or rough drink

indicators.note: something inside sits within the outer word, which wraps around it

blocks.note: to spy is to notice
c, circa, means about
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A sign warns about the strong liquor within, or perhaps something coarser to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrumpy is strong, cloudy farmhouse cider from the West Country of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is unrefined home-made cider, a rough and potent alcoholic drink from south-west England.

clue.text: Anger held back by girl in a row

held by someone means gripped within them, so the word sits inside the name

blocks.note: a girl's name
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A girl restrains her temper during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' wants to be a quarrel, but 'in a row' is the definition: one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Serially means one after another in a series, which is what happening in a row means.

clue.text: Form attachment, giving girl a kiss

blocks.note: a girl's name
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Form attachment' reads as falling in love; it is the verb to attach.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex is to attach or append something, as a territory or a document, which is forming an attachment.

clue.text: Watch for a vital organ

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a timepiece that ticks
second meaning: slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A doctor's instruction to keep an eye on an important body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb, to keep an eye on; it is the timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang both for a wristwatch, which ticks, and for the heart, which beats.

clue.text: Seafood can make king and queen poorly

blocks.note: K is the king in chess and cards
R is Regina, queen
poorly means ill

explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny shrimp-like crustaceans of the ocean, food for whales, so they count as seafood.

clue.text: Couch for a brief chat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Couch' looks like a sofa; it is the verb, to put into words.

clue.text: Prepared, thus, to keep dry wine

blocks.note: a mac, mackintosh, is a raincoat worn to stay dry

explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a wine from the area around the town of Mâcon in southern Burgundy, France.

clue.text: One new record is set by Mint's initial coinage _

the initial of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a log is a record
taken as written
the opening letter of Mint

explanation.surface: A new record is set by the Royal Mint's first coin issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' and 'coinage' make a picture of money; coinage here is a newly coined word. The trailing dots run on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly invented word or expression, which is what a coinage means in language.

clue.text: ... and this sort of record's seen in the long run

definitions.note: a describing phrase; the answer is the record type, an EP

blocks.note: first meaning: following on from the previous clue's record, a single-sized disc with extra tracks
second meaning: a stage show kept on for a long run

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a kind of record that shows up over time.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie it to 27: a new record there, a type of record here. 'In the long run' looks like 'eventually'; it is a theatre run.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended-play record holds more than a single but less than an LP, and a show with a long run gets extended play.
